note: FIXTURE-REQUIREMENTS.md's outstanding request ('f(*(a, b))' closes Gate 3) does not hold. Verified against the repo's own installed tree-sitter-python@0.21.0 (node_modules, not a throwaway build): 'f(*(a, b))' parses as list_splat(tuple(...)), never parenthesized_list_splat -- that node only appears when the '*' is INSIDE the parens as a direct list/set/tuple element (grammar site: _collection_elements, the only three call sites of that rule), e.g. '[(*x), 2]'. Exhaustively tried every reachable shape (list/set/tuple literal, with and without trailing comma, as a call argument, as an assignment RHS) via the real parser and cross-checked each against 3.10.4 ast.parse/compile. Every shape that actually produces a bare parenthesized_list_splat node -- '[(*x), 2]', '[(*x)]', 'y = (*x), 2' -- is rejected by CPython with SyntaxError: cannot use starred expression here. The only shapes CPython accepts either add a trailing comma (which changes the parse to tuple(list_splat(...)), not parenthesized_list_splat) or put the '*' before the parens (list_splat(parenthesized_expression(...))). Conclusion: parenthesized_list_splat appears UNREACHABLE under valid CPython 3.10.4 syntax, so per the corpus rule (ast.parse must accept it) it cannot be fixtured -- the 115 ceiling likely needs a further -1 to 114, matching FIXTURE-REQUIREMENTS.md's OWN measured 114/115 before this residual item was raised. Escalating rather than deciding, per README: this changes Gate 3's stated bar and is A0's call, not mine.

Second unreachable-node finding, same shape as the parenthesized_list_splat one above. tree-sitter-python@0.21.0's grammar defines type: choice(expression, splat_type, generic_type, union_type, constrained_type, member_type) with union_type: type '|' type. Exhaustively probed every syntactic position where 'type' is used (typed_parameter, annotated assignment x: T = v, return type -> T, generic subscript's inner type list[X | Y], and even the PEP 695 type-alias RHS 'type X = int | str') using the real installed parser (node_modules/tree-sitter-python, not a throwaway build). In every single case, 'X | Y' in type position reduces to expression's binary_operator (bitwise-or), never to union_type -- there is no conflict/prec.dynamic entry favoring union_type, so it appears permanently shadowed by the expression alternative and is dead grammar in this version, the same situation STOPPING-CONDITION.md already documented for member_type ('unreachable: no probe produces it, including PEP 695 type contexts and every dotted-annotation form'). If confirmed, the reachable ceiling is 113, not 115 (114 minus the already-open parenthesized_list_splat finding minus this one) -- staging/native is at 113/113 on that basis. Escalating rather than deciding, per README; this and the parenthesized_list_splat finding should probably be resolved together.

summary: Oracle harness (src/test/python-oracle/oracle/emit_oracle.py, _pair_children) silently mis-pairs same-line nested comprehensions, swapping which ast node -> which symtable scope. It does NOT raise a PAIRING_UNMATCHED problem, so `--oracle <file>` self-check reports clean (0 errors) even though the emitted scope/binding facts are WRONG. This was found via src/test/python-scratch/diff-oracle.ts (extractor vs oracle), not via the self-check path -- the self-check alone cannot catch this class of bug.
observed: diff-oracle reports the OUTER comprehension's scope (col 11, binds q) gets the ORACLE's binding for `r`, and the INNER comprehension's scope (col 23, binds r) gets the oracle's binding for `q` -- fully swapped, plus scopeOrdinal swapped to match (oracle: col11=ordinal7,col23=ordinal8; the correct/extractor side has it the other way). Confirmed this is the extractor's behavior that is RIGHT, not wrong: traced python-scope-builder.ts visitComprehension (lines ~1537-1599) line by line -- Rule 1 evaluates the outer iterable (which recurses into the inner comprehension, creating ITS scope via createChildBlock with the inner ListComp's own node/position) BEFORE createChildBlock runs for the outer comprehension's own scope, and each createChildBlock call correctly stamps startLine/startColumn from the specific node passed to THAT call. No swap is possible on the extractor side from this code path.
root_cause: emit_oracle.py _pair_children (line ~183-219) pairs symtable children to ast candidates by filtering on (type, name, lineno) then picking `min(cands, key=col_offset)` -- a greedy leftmost-column tie-break. That tie-break assumes symtable's per-scope CREATION order corresponds to ascending column order among same-line/type/name candidates. It does for independent same-line siblings (already tested and correct: 'g = (lambda: 1, lambda: 2)', 'h = [x for x in [1]] + [y for y in [2]]' both pass diff-oracle clean). It does NOT hold when one same-line/type/name candidate is nested inside another's `_enclosing_evaluated_parts` (i.e., is literally the outer comprehension's own iterable) -- symtable there creates the INNER (higher-column) scope's table FIRST (because compiling the outer's iterable expression recursively compiles the inner comprehension in full before the outer comprehension's own sub-scope is entered), but the tie-break greedily assigns the smallest column (the OUTER node) to that first symtable child instead, silently swapping the pairing for both same-line nested scopes. _owned_scope_nodes already has the true nesting relationship in hand at construction time (it discovers the inner node specifically via recursion into the outer node's _enclosing_evaluated_parts, see lines ~159-176) but that structural information is discarded by the final flat `found.sort(key=(lineno,col_offset))`, so _pair_children has no way to recover it and falls back to the column heuristic.
trigger_scope: Requires BOTH comprehensions to share the same source lineno (confirmed: moving the inner comprehension to its own line makes the bug disappear, since the lineno filter alone then disambiguates candidates) AND a nesting relationship where one is literally the other's outermost iterable (confirmed: two INDEPENDENT same-line same-type comprehensions, not nested in each other, pair correctly). A realistic trigger -- exactly what an auto-formatter produces for a short nested comprehension.
why_not_staged_as_fixture: Self-check via `npx tsx src/test/python-oracle/run.ts --oracle <file>` reports 0 errors on the repro (verified) because _pair_children raises no PAIRING_UNMATCHED problem -- it just picks the wrong candidate silently. Per protocol I only stage fixtures that fail loudly when wrong; staging this now would look like a normal clean fixture and bury the defect instead of surfacing it. Recommending A0 fix _pair_children first (e.g., preserve the parent/child discovery order from _owned_scope_nodes's recursion instead of re-deriving order from a flat column sort, or special-case: an ast candidate found via recursion into another candidate's _enclosing_evaluated_parts must be paired to whichever symtable child is NOT the one already claimed by an ancestor pairing pass), then this repro should be promoted to a permanent regression fixture in staging/native once the fix lands.

summary: python-declaration-extractor.ts classifyType()/typeModifiersOf() (Stage 2, class-declaration extraction) silently misclassify classes that use the metaclass= KEYWORD argument instead of direct inheritance for ABC/Enum -- a real, common idiom, not a contrived one. Directly relevant to the 'Enum class' hint: functional/metaclass-style Enum declarations are completely missed.
root_cause: python-declaration-extractor.ts classifyType() (~line 493-531) computes baseNames from `bases.filter(b => b.keywordName === '')` -- i.e. it DROPS every keyword base (metaclass=, total=) before checking for ABC/Enum/etc name matches, so a class expressing its metaclass via `metaclass=ABCMeta`/`metaclass=EnumMeta` instead of direct inheritance is invisible to this function entirely. typeModifiersOf() (~line 534-583), operating on the SAME bases array, does NOT filter out keyword bases (`baseNames = bases.map(...)` with no .filter), so its ABC check (`n === 'ABC' || n === 'ABCMeta'`) DOES see metaclass=ABCMeta and correctly sets the ABSTRACT modifier -- but has no equivalent check for EnumMeta at all. Net effect: two functions reading the identical bases array disagree on whether a keyword-expressed metaclass counts, and neither one recognizes EnumMeta as an Enum signal in any form.
impact: Silent misclassification (wrong typeCategory, not a crash or loud failure) for a real-world idiom -- `metaclass=ABCMeta` predates and remains common alongside `abc.ABC` (needed when a class needs an unrelated existing metaclass mixed with ABCMeta, or in code that hasn't adopted the ABC convenience base), and `metaclass=EnumMeta` is how you write an Enum-like class when you need functionality Enum's own __new__ doesn't provide. Also produces an internally inconsistent fact set for the ABCMeta case: typeModifier=ABSTRACT but typeCategory=CLASS_TYPE for the same row.
oracle_gap: NEITHER gate can currently catch this even after a fix: emit_oracle.py's _collect_structure/visit_ClassDef (~line 440-454) captures only bases[].kind/text and decorators[] as raw text -- it emits no typeCategory or typeModifier field at all, and diff-decl.ts (the Gate-2 declaration differ) does not compare typeCategory/typeModifier either (only endLine and positional baseCount, ~line 42-44). So this class of bug is invisible to both the self-check oracle AND the differential diff tool; it was only found by invoking PythonFactExtractor directly and eyeballing output against hand-derived expectations. Flagging for A0: if typeCategory/typeModifier are meant to be oracle-adjudicated at all (they are ast-derivable, in principle Gate-2 territory per the schema's own layer-2 definition), _collect_structure needs to also capture ast.ClassDef.keywords (already visits n.keywords for bases[] but only for the base-count check, not surfaced as a re-checkable metaclass field) and diff-decl.ts needs a typeCategory/typeModifier comparison added.
suggested_fix_direction: Not mine to implement (src/parsers/python is A3's). classifyType() should inspect the metaclass= keyword base's value (rightmost name) with the SAME regex/equality checks it already applies to positional bases, rather than filtering keyword bases out entirely; typeModifiersOf() should add an EnumMeta check alongside its existing ABC/ABCMeta check for consistency.
